description:
El regreso del ser humano a la Luna y las futuras misiones a Marte exigen llevar la seguridad en el espacio a un nuevo nivel. Durante décadas, la NASA ha acumulado una inmensa base de datos sobre la física del fuego y la combustión en microgravedad. Sin embargo, el enorme volumen de información dispersa dificulta que ingenieros y científicos puedan extraer conclusiones rápidas para diseñar misiones seguras.

Nuestro objetivo es construir un dashboard interactivo impulsado por Inteligencia Artificial capaz de sintetizar, clasificar y predecir el comportamiento del fuego en microgravedad, transformando décadas de datos experimentales de la NASA en recomendaciones accionables de ingeniería para la exploración espacial profunda.
summary: "Martian Map" is an interactive map of the entirety of Mars. It shows information about its temperature, topography, frozen regions, geographical points of interest, a reconstruction of the planet in the past and a representation of a plausible future colonization. Moreover, it serves as a guide for future expeditions in Jezero, Gale, and Arcadia, with an interactive way of finding the safest and most efficient route between two points. This way of processing information can be relevant for the astronauts, as it makes it easy to comprehend and can simplify the complex and abstract information current maps of Mars carry within them.
details:
This project is an interactive map inspired by apps that cartography the whole Earth such as Google Earth. There are two main ways of using this map.

The first part is really interesting for astronauts. Toghether with an history of past missions there are three representations of small areas in which we have focused to provide a service to help the navigation. These areas are Jezero, Gale and Arcadia. We have chosen these areas because there are the ones with more useful information we posses currently. We know exactly the topography, points of scientifical interest and how to make safe routes.

In this mode there are two points you can move with your cursor, so they mark an start, end and any stop that you want. Then, the map will calculate the safest (less than 10º slope) and fastest route and give the data considerating the velocity and capacitys of a rover and the average speed of a human. The map will also show points with an excessive slope and interest points nearby, which you can select and add a new spot to the route. You can also manipulate the overview of the map, so you can hide or show the clouds, the conditions of temperature, the ice in 1m depth, the topography and the rugosity. Moreover, you can change the multipliers for the topography either near it or far away. Furthermore, in this window you can specifie the characteristics of the mission (nº of astronauts, the maximum slope considered, the rover, the time you want to stay in each stop...) so it can adjust to the needs of of the expedition with flexibility in its variables.

This is the mode that is most interesting, because it presents in a visual and easy way the complex terrain of an area in Mars, therefore, it is a great way to plan, analyze and take decisions easily and rapidly, with the benefits of having a visual guide. It would also be useful in the exploration itself making easy to recognise possible hazards and choose the best paths. It also shows a graph with the conditions of the path, temperature, slope, and other relevant information, in which you can select the moment and look for its charasteristics at said moment.

We have considered that the most relevant parts to analyze are the temperature and topography for the preparation of the mission, in addition, places with ice within a meter depth, mineral ores and relevant topographical elements as points of interest for the mission itself. In this window, you can also see how much time the expedition would last by rover or by rover and feet, with other additional information such as the speed, and numerical information of the path.

The other mode consists on a map of the whole planet, which we can't do with such a detailed information as the one put in the three areas we have highlighted before, because of the lack of proper data and time to analyze it.

There are a few things that are worth mentioning, in this mode there is a prefixed multiplier of scale for the representation of the topography in 3d of 8.5, for it to be more noticeable. Also, for divulgative purposes we have included a guideline of the history of Mars and a possible future, which are represented with their own lakes, vegetation and even cities. In this mode there is a button called layers, in which you can manipulate the map in a way very similar to the map of the detailed area.

The purpose of this mode is for the astronauts and scientifics to comprehend and view an approximation of the reality on the surface on mars, without too much complexity, and helping them visualize the abstract and otherways complicated data that is represented in usual maps.

Knowing that we have an overall faithful representation of the planet, if we could have the detailed data of the entire surface, the treatment of the areas could have been done, thus ensuring a great way to calculate really long expeditions.
